title: Story project
description: A branching interactive story: pages, choices, things the player carries, numbers, dice checks and start-of-story questions. This is the shape the Story Editor saves. Only `passages` is required; normalizeProject() fills in every other field and removes anything broken, so hand-written or AI-written files may leave fields out. Ids are short strings (letters, digits, _ and -, up to 64 characters). A page whose `ending` is true shows no choices.

rev.description: revision counter, raised by one each time the editor saves the story to a file (display only; the game never reads it)

savedAt.description: UTC time of the last save to a file, as 2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z (display only)

start.description: id of the first page (defaults to the first page in the list)

lang0c.description: language code of the story's own language (for example es or ar); sets lang and reading direction in the game, and is left out for English

lang0.description: what the story's own language is called (defaults to English); the first choice in the game's language menu

langs.description: Translations. Each language maps the exact (trimmed, LF-only) source text of a page, choice, item or label to its translation; anything not listed stays as written. Present languages add a language menu to the exported game.

code.description: optional language tag such as es or pt-BR

gameFont.description: use the reader's own font in the exported game (smaller file)

game.description: Reader options for the exported game. Only non-default values need to be present.

back.description: a Back button; for dice checks it can remember the old roll, roll again, or be blocked

tracker.description: show 'endings found' and remember them on the reader's device

comfort.description: the Aa button (text size, spacing, contrast, calm motion)

odds.description: show the chance of success on dice checks

place.description: a copyable code that returns a reader to their place

items.description: Things the player can carry (object), conditions they can be in (state), or numbers (stat).

start.description: stat only: value at the start

names.description: show the item under another name while the player has or is `when`

givens.description: Questions asked before page one. The reader's answer becomes a state they are in for the whole story.

name.description: the author's name for the page (never shown to the reader)

heading.description: shown above the text; for an ending, its title

valence.description: for endings: good, bad, or neutral (empty)

note.description: the author's private note on the page (never exported)

orPrev.description: show only if the paragraph above was hidden

sends.description: where a lost object went: 'here' or 'w:<name of who got it>'

to.description: id of the page it leads to ('' = nowhere yet)

oneOf.description: a dice check: roll two six-sided dice, add the player's `stat`; reaching `target` goes to the choice's page, otherwise to `fail`

lock.description: show greyed out (with `why`) while its conditions are not met, instead of hiding it

ids.description: item ids; a stat condition is written t:<statId>:<n> and means 'the stat is n or more'

adds.description: { statId: number } to add (negative to subtract)
